newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt largely unchanged after soft retail sales.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt largely unchanged after soft retail sales.

text.p: New Zealand debt markets were largely unmoved by soft March quarter retail trade data on Friday, having expected the number to confirm the picture of a weak economy.
Statistics New Zealand (SNZ) said seasonally adjusted retail sales fell one percent in the March quarter, following a fall of 0.3 percent in the December quarter.
Actual sales fell two percent against the March 1996 quarter, which SNZ said was the first annual fall in actual sales for 20 consecutive quarters.
Dealers noted the dramatic $280 million (15.2 percent) fall in the value of sales in motor vehicle retailing in the year to the March quarter.
"Car sales were much weaker than expected. Once those were taken out, it was actually a relatively a strong number," one said.

He added that a few offshore traders bought the market initially, expecting the small rally to kick on, but that didn't occur and the money market soon stabilised again at levels slightly stronger than its Thursday closing levels.
By noon the 90-day bank bills were at 7.01 percent, against their 7.03 percent close on Thursday. The June futures contract was up five basis points at 92.89.

Earlier in the session, before the data's release, a money market dealer said he didn't expect the market to rally far if the seasonally adjusted retail sales out-turn came in on his bank's expectations of a 0.5 percent fall.
"I think we're just too close to the parameters where the Reserve Bank don't want monetary conditions to ease too much further," he commented.

Meanwhile, local bonds are treading water ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's next meeting on May 20, with the U.S. Treasury market hoping the Fed will not feel the urge to lift official interest rates once more.
